 by Cricbuzz Staff •     Share Tweet The big IPL trade © AFP The big IPL trade © AFP Hardik Pandya, captain of Mumbai Indians for the last three seasons, will move to Punjab Kings in a player trade ahead of the 2027 Indian Premier League, with India pacer Arshdeep Singh heading the other way in a straight swap between the two franchises. The trade, which had been in the works for over a week, has now been formally approved by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI).
 Pandya will join PBKS at a fee of INR 18 crore, up from his existing fee of INR 16.35 crore, while Arshdeep will move to MI at his existing fee of INR 18 crore. The deal brings to an end Pandya's second stint with Mumbai, where he returned in 2024 and took over the captaincy after leading Gujarat Titans to the title in their debut season in 2022.
 Pandya first joined MI in 2015 and was part of four title-winning campaigns with the franchise (2015, 2017, 2019 and 2020). He subsequently moved to Gujarat Titans ahead of the 2022 season, leading them to the title in their inaugural campaign and the final in 2023. Across 162 IPL appearances, the all-rounder has scored 2,955 runs at a strike rate of 146.28 and taken 82 wickets.
 Arshdeep, meanwhile, brings an eight-season association with Punjab Kings to a close. Having made his IPL debut for the franchise in 2019, the left-arm pacer went on to become their all-time leading wicket-taker, with 111 wickets from 96 matches. He picked up 21 wickets in IPL 2025 and followed it up with 14 in the 2026 season. He is also India's leading wicket-taker in T20 Internationals.
 As previously reported by Cricbuzz , the proposed trade had progressed to the final stages after the two franchises exchanged Expressions of Interest (EoIs) with the BCCI. The process, however, encountered a brief delay as the players took time to consider and provide their consent. Both eventually agreed to the move, with the formal approval from the board following thereafter.
 The trade addresses a key requirement for Mumbai, who had been looking to add a quality pace option to complement Jasprit Bumrah. Arshdeep's ability to strike with the new ball and operate effectively at the death is expected to strengthen their bowling attack. For the Shreyas Iyer-led Punjab team, which reached the IPL final in 2025, Pandya adds an experienced Indian all-rounder with a proven record of delivering in high-pressure situations.
